Entry God-Emperors of Yi Ti The Emperor of Yi Di is often understood as the "God Emperor" or a title connected with heaven. His status comes not only from the army, but also from the imagination of maintaining the order of the universe and the world. The court regarded this title as orthodox, and ordinary people were more concerned about whether this man sitting far away could bring stability. Altars, relics, and prophecies can unite people and give a political claim the appearance of irrefutability.

Entry God-Emperors of Yi Ti The Emperor of Yi Di is often understood as the "God Emperor" or a title connected with heaven. His status comes not only from the army, but also from the imagination of maintaining the order of the universe and the world. The court regarded this title as orthodox, and ordinary people were more concerned about whether this man sitting far away could bring stability. Some people use it as a talisman, while others use it as the name of fear; the same prayer may make people draw their swords or put them down.

Entry God-Emperors of Yi Ti The Emperor of Yi Di is often understood as the "God Emperor" or a title connected with heaven. His status comes not only from the army, but also from the imagination of maintaining the order of the universe and the world. The court regarded this title as orthodox, and ordinary people were more concerned about whether this man sitting far away could bring stability. Whether the gods responded or not could not be proven by the account books, but how the rituals were held and who could interpret the omens actually determined the authority of the community.

They seek an explanation they can rely on when it comes to birth, marriage, sowing, illness, and death; the names of gods may not be the same, but their desire to keep their families safe is similar.
